title: Nintendo Switch Repair
subtitle: Not charging, no signs of life at all.
description: Last week, my kids' Nintendo Switch completely died and refused to charge. I found a short on the M92T36 power management IC, micro-soldered a replacement chip, and now it's working again

WhatsApp Image 2026-09-19 at 18.17.46.jp: My Yojock meter isn't powering on, which confirms the Switch motherboard is drawing zero power.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-19 at 18.32.39.jp: The M92T36 is the power management chip for the Nintendo Switch.
Screenshot 2026-09-19 at 18.25.16.png: I ordered a brand new M92T36 chip from MBI Tech Parts, a family owned supplier based in Donegal, Ireland.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-19 at 18.10.10.jp: I tested the battery with a multimeter and found that while the charge is very low, it is still healthy.
2026-09-27 at 15.29.00.MOV: I removed the M92T36 Charge Control Chip using my rework station.
WhatsApp Image 2026-09-27 at 15.30.54.jp: Then I cleaned everything up using 99.9% IPA and these new nano-cleaning sponges. They are so much better than the cotton buds I had been using until now because they don't leave annoying strands of fiber behind!
WhatsApp Video 2026-09-27 at 16.08.53.mp: New theory: the USBC port needs to be replaced.
2026-09-28 at 15.10.00.MOV: Clean-up time! I used plenty of 99.9% IPA along with some brand new tools to replace the terrible cotton buds I was using previously.
2026-09-28 at 15.00.00.MOV: I decided to remove the USB-C port. My 3rd time using a rework station.
2026-09-28 at 15.20.00.JPG: The VBUS short (Pin 9 of the M92T36) is gone now, so the USB-C port was the real root cause all along.

From what I've read online, normally when a USB-C port needs to be replaced like mine did, it's already too late for the M92T36 IC because it likely received a voltage spike and blew up, requiring replacement as well.
WhatsApp Video 2026-09-26 at 18.35.08.mp: A dead short on the capacitor across pins 8 (GND) and 9 (VBUS), possibly caused by the M92T36 being shorted internally?"
6f45a7c0911ee30f1d647e5edf7d354203fdfd06: The short I am using is that Pin 9 (VBUS) is being pulled to GND
IMG_008.JPG: Added some flux so that I can tin the new USB-C port
IMG_009.JPG: Tinned and ready to be installed
IMG_011.JPG: I'm not entirely happy with the solder around the four anchor points, but for my current level of experience, it's not too bad.
IMG_012.JPG:
Good news: I managed to install the new M92T36 chip. 
Bad news: My hand was so shaky that I knocked at least five components off their pads while trying to place it.
IMG_017.JPG: Only one at the top of the chip but that is also going to need re-alignment.
